episodes.200476: A midlevel trough and an associated surface cold front progressed from the Appalachians into the Atlantic coast. A few strong wind gusts were associated with this activity.
episodes.200592: An ice jam on the Aroostook River between Caribou and Fort Fairfield led to flooding which closed portions of the North Caribou Road and Strickland Road. This ice jam developed during the evening of the 20th and persisted into the afternoon of the 26th. A second ice jam developed near Wade during the morning of the 21st and persisted into the morning of the 27th. This ice jam led to flooding along Gardner Creek Road and other low lying areas bordering the river. The ice jam isolated several camp properties due to high water. The ice jam released during the morning of the 27th allowing river levels to fall.
episodes.200867: Two men were fishing on southern Lake Michigan near East Chicago's steel mill when their 19-foot vessel capsized during the afternoon of the 21st. One man was able to swim to shore and was transported to a local hospital where he recovered. The other man, a 73 year old, did not survive and his body was recovered later that afternoon. A Gale Warning was in effect at the time advertising hazardous boating conditions. The Harrison-Dever Crib was consistently reporting 50 to 55 mph gusts at the time of the incident and the water temperature was recorded nearby at 37 degrees.
